claims.text: A controlled sub-critical anneal can introduce short-range chemical order into equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
The annealing-induced short-range order will take the form of nanoscale clusters.
Local chemical ordering or associated chemical heterogeneities can pin or hinder dislocations.
Annealing-induced short-range order will increase the yield strength of equimolar CoCrFeNiTi relative to its as-cast state.
Annealing-induced short-range order will increase the hardness of equimolar CoCrFeNiTi relative to its as-cast state.
As-cast, nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi is a fully random solid solution.
As-cast, nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi is single phase.
Annealing CoCrFeNiTi at approximately 700°C for 4–6 hours can produce only short-range order without secondary-phase precipitation.
The random as-cast atomic distribution provides few obstacles to dislocation motion.
A low density of dislocation obstacles governs the low strength and hardness of the starting CoCrFeNiTi state.
Short-range chemical ordering alters local bonding environments.
Dominant local chemical order increases dislocation activation barriers and critical resolved shear stress.
Dislocation pinning by the induced order will enhance strain hardening.
The SRO-treated material will develop a higher density of more complex, tangled dislocation networks during deformation.

The applicable domain is room-temperature tensile, compression, and nanoindentation testing of single-phase equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi at quasi-static to moderate strain rates and below transformation or precipitation thresholds.
The low-hardness, low-strength as-cast state has favorable plasticity and machinability.
Annealing intended to create chemical order carries a risk of producing precipitates or compositional decomposition.
TEM and XRD can verify the presence of short-range order while excluding secondary precipitation in the treated samples.
A statistically nonsignificant change in yield strength, hardness, or strain-hardening rate relative to the as-cast control is specified as a falsifying result.
Observation of secondary precipitates rather than solely short-range order is specified as falsifying the proposed SRO-strengthening hypothesis.
